paragraphs: Friend, here's what David teaches me in Psalm 69. When the water is up to your neck, you don't have to pretend you're fine. David says it plain: "Save me, O God, for the waters are up to my neck." He tells God about the mire, the haters and the shame, and he even admits, "You know my folly, O God, and my guilt is not hidden from You." (Psalm 69:1, 5)

Now look at where David's hope sits. It isn't on his spotless record. It's on God's character: "In Your abundant loving devotion, O God, answer me with Your sure salvation." (Psalm 69:13) Even in the heavy part, when David asks God to deal with his enemies, he turns right back and says, "But I am in pain and distress; let Your salvation protect me, O God." (Psalm 69:29) I think that's a gift for us, baker. You can bring God the whole mess, the hurt AND the anger, and you leave it with Him.

And the psalm doesn't end in the water. David says, "I will praise God's name in song and exalt Him with thanksgiving," and then tells us why: "For the LORD listens to the needy and does not despise His captive people." (Psalm 69:30, 33) So when you're sinking, pray, because He listens. And when He lifts you, sing, because you've got a song of your own now.
